46949-chats-on-costume.title: Chats On Costume
46949-chats-on-costume.creator: Arthur Hayden
46949-chats-on-costume.description: A book by Arthur Hayden. "You see two individuals, one dressed in fine Red, the other  in coarse threadbare Blue: Red says to Blue: 'Be hanged and  anatomised;' Blue hears with a shudder, and (O wonder of wonders!)  marches sorrowfully to the gallows; is there noosed-up, vibrates  his hour, and the surgeons dissect him, and fit his bones into a  skeleton for medical purposes.

arxiv-2012-11987.title: Unsupervised Functional Data Analysis via Nonlinear Dimension Reduction
arxiv-2012-11987.creator: Moritz Herrmann, Fabian Scheipl
arxiv-2012-11987.description: Abstract In recent years, manifold methods have moved into focus as tools for dimension reduction. Assuming that the high-dimensional data actually lie on or close to a low-dimensional nonlinear manifold, these methods have shown convincing results in several settings. This manifold assumption is often reasonable for functional data, i.e., data representing continuously observed functions, as well.

arxiv-2201-09148.title: The earliest O-type eclipsing binary in the Small Magellanic Cloud, AzV 476: A comprehensive analysis reveals surprisingly low stellar masses
arxiv-2201-09148.creator: D. Pauli 1, L. M. Oskinova 1, W.-R. Hamann 1, V. Ramachandran 1,3, H. Todt 1, A. A. C. Sander 2,3, T. Shenar 4, M. Rickard 1,5, J. Maíz Apellániz 6, R. Prinja 5
arxiv-2201-09148.description: Abstract Context. Massive stars at low metallicity are among the main feedback agents in the early Universe and in present-day star forming galaxies. When in binaries, these stars are potential progenitors of gravitational-wave events. Knowledge of stellar masses is a prerequisite to understanding evolution and feedback of low-metallicity massive stars. Aims.

arxiv-2204-12084.title: U-Net with ResNet Backbone for Garment Landmarking Purpose
arxiv-2204-12084.creator: Kelvin Hong Khay Boon
arxiv-2204-12084.description: Abstract We build a heatmap-based landmark detection model to locate important landmarks on 2D RGB garment images. The main goal is to detect edges, corners and suitable interior region of the garments. This let us re-create 3D garments in modern 3D editing software by incorporate landmark detection model and texture unwrapping.

arxiv-2306-02176.title: TransRUPNet for Improved Polyp Segmentation
arxiv-2306-02176.creator: Debesh Jha, Nikhil Kumar Tomar, Debayan Bhattacharya, Koushik Biswas, Ulas BagciMachine & Hybrid Intelligence Lab, Department of Radiology, Northwestern UniversityInstitute of Medical Technology and Intelligent System, Hamburg University of Technology& Clinic for Ears, Nose and Throat, University Me
arxiv-2306-02176.description: Abstract Colorectal cancer is among the most common cause of cancer worldwide. Removal of precancerous polyps through early detection is essential to prevent them from progressing to colon cancer. We develop an advanced deep learning-based architecture, Transformer based Residual Upsampling Network (TransRUPNet) for automatic and real-time polyp segmentation.

arxiv-2309-09141.title: Event-based Compositional Reasoning of Information-Flow Security for Concurrent Systems Conference: POPL 2016 Submission July, 2016
arxiv-2309-09141.description: Abstract High assurance of information-flow security (IFS) for concurrent systems is challenging. A promising way for formal verification of concurrent systems is the rely-guarantee method. However, existing compositional reasoning approaches for IFS concentrate on language-based IFS. It is often not applicable for system-level security, such as multicore operating system kernels, in which secrecy of actions should also be considered.

arxiv-2407-12456.title: Seasonal Changes in the Atmosphere of HD 80606 b {\rm b} Observed with JWST’s NIRSpec/G395H Facilities: JWST (NIRSpec)
arxiv-2407-12456.creator: James T. Sikora, Jason F. Rowe, Jared Splinter, Saugata Barat, Lisa Dang, Nicolas B. Cowan, Thomas Barclay, Knicole D. Colón, Jean-Michel Désert, Stephen R. Kane, Joe Llama, Hinna Shivkumar, Keivan G. Stassun, Elisa V. Quintana
arxiv-2407-12456.description: Abstract High-eccentricity gas giant planets serve as unique laboratories for studying the thermal and chemical properties of H/He-dominated atmospheres. One of the most extreme cases is HD 80606b—a hot Jupiter orbiting a sun-like star with an eccentricity of 0.93 0.93 —which experiences an increase in incident flux of nearly three orders of magnitude as the star-planet separation decreases from 0.

arxiv-2410-02798.title: Joint multifractality in the cross-correlations between grains & oilseeds indices and external uncertainties
arxiv-2410-02798.creator: Ying-Hui Shao, Xing-Lu Gao, Yan-Hong Yang, Wei-Xing Zhou
arxiv-2410-02798.description: Abstract This study investigates the relationships between agricultural spot markets and external uncertainties via the multifractal detrending moving-average cross-correlation analysis (MF-X-DMA). The dataset contains the Grains & Oilseeds Index (GOI) and its five sub-indices of wheat, maize, soyabeans, rice, and barley. Moreover, we use three uncertainty proxies, namely, economic policy uncertainty (EPU), geopolitical risk (GPR), and volatility Index (VIX).

arxiv-2412-04839.title: Classical-quantum scattering
arxiv-2412-04839.creator: Daniel Carney, Akira Matsumura
arxiv-2412-04839.description: Abstract We analyze the framework recently proposed by Oppenheim et al. to model relativistic quantum fields coupled to relativistic, classical, stochastic fields (in particular, as a model of quantum matter coupled to “classical gravity”). Perhaps surprisingly, we find that we can define and calculate scattering probabilities which are Lorentz-covariant and conserve total probability, at least at tree level.

arxiv-2508-11235.title: Enhancing Interactive Voting-Based Map Matching: Improving Efficiency and Robustness for Heterogeneous GPS Trajectories
arxiv-2508-11235.creator: William Alemanni, Arianna Burzacchi, Davide Colombi, Elena Giarratano
arxiv-2508-11235.description: Abstract This paper presents an enhanced version of the Interactive Voting-Based Map Matching algorithm, designed to efficiently process trajectories with varying sampling rates. The main aim is to reconstruct GPS trajectories with high accuracy, independent of input data quality. Building upon the original algorithm, developed exclusively for aligning GPS signals to road networks—we extend its capabilities by integrating trajectory imputation.

arxiv-2509-09653.title: Towards A High-Performance Quantum Data Center Network Architecture
arxiv-2509-09653.creator: Yufeng Xin, Liang Zhang
arxiv-2509-09653.description: Abstract Quantum Data Centers (QDCs) are needed to support large-scale quantum processing for both academic and commercial applications. While large-scale quantum computers are constrained by technological and financial barriers, a modular approach that clusters small quantum computers offers an alternative. This approach, however, introduces new challenges in network scalability, entanglement generation, and quantum memory management.

arxiv-2509-16194.title: Clustering with Set Outliers and Applications in Relational Clustering CCS: Theory of computation Database theory CCS: Theory of computation Data structures and algorithms for data management
arxiv-2509-16194.creator: Vaishali Surianarayanan, Neeraj Kumar, Stavros Sintos
arxiv-2509-16194.description: Abstract . We introduce and study the k k -center clustering problem with set outliers , a natural and practical generalization of the classical k k -center clustering with outliers. Instead of removing individual data points, our model allows discarding up to z z subsets from a given family of candidate outlier sets ℋ \mathcal{H} .

arxiv-2510-06849.title: Extending Ghouila-Houri’s Characterization of Comparability Graphs to Temporal Graphs Thanks: This work was supported by the French ANR projects ANR-24-CE48-4377 (GODASse) and ANR-22-CE48-0001 (TEMPOGRAL).
arxiv-2510-06849.creator: Pierre Charbit, Michel Habib, Amalia Sorondo
arxiv-2510-06849.description: Abstract An orientation of a static graph is called transitive if for any three vertices a , b , c a,b,c , the presence of arcs ( a , b ) (a,b) and ( b , c ) (b,c) forces the presence of arc ( a , c ) (a,c) .

arxiv-2510-14789.title: Quantum confinement of scalar bosons in the Bonnor-Melvin spacetime: uniform magnetic field and rainbow gravity effects
arxiv-2510-14789.creator: Omar Mustafa, Abdullah Guvendi
arxiv-2510-14789.description: Abstract We present an exact analytical study of Klein-Gordon (KG) scalar bosons and antibosons confined in the Bonnor-Melvin (BM) spacetime under a uniform magnetic field, incorporating rainbow gravity (RG) corrections with a positive cosmological constant. The cosmological constant partitions spacetime into an infinite sequence of confinement domains bounded by impenetrable barriers.

arxiv-2510-25367.title: Self-organization, Memory and Learning: From Driven Disordered Systems to Living Matter Journal: Xxxx. Xxx. Xxx. Xxx. DOI: 10.1146/((please add article doi))
arxiv-2510-25367.creator: Muhittin Mungan 1, Eric Clément 2,3, Damien Vandembroucq 3 and Srikanth Sastry 4
arxiv-2510-25367.description: Abstract Disordered systems subject to a fluctuating environment can self-organize into a complex history-dependent response, retaining a memory of the driving. In sheared amorphous solids, self-organization is established by the emergence of a persistent system of mechanical instabilities that can repeatedly be triggered by the driving, leading to a state of high mechanical reversibility.

arxiv-2601-22666.title: ExpAlign: Expectation-Guided Vision–Language Alignment for Open-Vocabulary Grounding
arxiv-2601-22666.creator: Junyi Hu, Tian Bai, Fengyi Wu, Wenyan Li, Zhenming Peng, Yi Zhang
arxiv-2601-22666.description: Abstract Open-vocabulary grounding requires accurate vision-language alignment under weak supervision, yet existing methods either rely on global sentence embeddings that lack fine-grained expressiveness or introduce token-level alignment with explicit supervision or heavy cross-attention designs. We propose ExpAlign , a theoretically grounded vision-language alignment framework built on a principled multiple instance learning formulation.

pmc-10735668.title: THE LONELINESS OF LOW-INCOME OLDER ADULTS IN A FEDERAL VOLUNTEERING PROGRAM: A MIXED-METHOD NETWORK PERSPECTIVE
pmc-10735668.creator: Katy (Qiuchang) Cao
pmc-10735668.description: Volunteering is considered an important way to prevent and address loneliness for community-living older adults by fostering social interactions. However, some social network studies conducted outside of the volunteering context suggest that increased interactions among lonely individuals can elevate network members’ loneliness through the co-rumination of negative emotions.

pmc-11436654.title: Nomogram predicting overall and cancer specific prognosis for poorly differentiated lung adenocarcinoma after resection based on SEER cohort analysis
pmc-11436654.creator: Weijian Song, Jianwei Shi, Boxuan Zhou, Xiangzhi Meng, Mei Liang, Yushun Gao
pmc-11436654.description: The prognosis of poorly differentiated lung adenocarcinoma (PDLA) is determined by many clinicopathological factors. The aim of this study is identifying prognostic factors and developing reliable nomogram to predict the overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) in patients with PDLA. Patient data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results (SEER) database was collected and analyzed.

pmc-11443984.title: Advancing Public Health Surveillance in Child Care Centers: Stakeholder-Informed Redesign and User Satisfaction Evaluation of the MCRISP Network
pmc-11443984.creator: William Gribbin, Peter Dejonge, Jakob Rodseth, Andrew Hashikawa, Amaryllis Mavragani
pmc-11443984.description: Leveraging user feedback, we redesigned a novel disease monitoring utility to allow for bidirectional data flow and in this letter offer insights into that process as well as lessons learned. Introduction Child care centers are important hubs for monitoring respiratory and gastrointestinal illness transmission [1,2].

pmc-11454566.title: 5120 Contribution Of Proximal Femur Geometry And Bone Density Distribution To Hip Fragility In Adults ≥ 50yrs With Longstanding Type 1 Diabetes
pmc-11454566.creator: F Johannesdottir, C D’Mello, A B Murthy, B Zahedi, K Engelke, M L Bouxsein, E W Yu
pmc-11454566.description: Disclosure: F. Johannesdottir: None. C. D’Mello: None. A.B. Murthy: None. B. Zahedi: None. K. Engelke: None. M.L. Bouxsein: None. E.W. Yu: Grant Recipient; Self; Amgen Inc. Introduction: Adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) have a 6-fold increased risk of hip fracture, which is explained only in part by lower areal bone mineral density (aBMD) by DXA.

pmc-11486895.title: Prognostic value of the fat-free mass index-based cachexia index in patients with colorectal cancer
pmc-11486895.creator: Yating Qin, Hailun Xie, Tong Liu, Heyang Zhang, Chenan Liu, Xiangrui Li, Zhaoting Bu, Xiaoyue Liu, Shiqi Lin, Yue Chen, Xin Zheng, Hong Zhao, Jinyu Shi, Hanping Shi
pmc-11486895.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Studies have shown that the cachexia index (CXI) is a useful predictor of cachexia in patients with colorectal cancer. However, the application of the CXI is limited stemming from the intricacy and additional cost of radiographic examinations. This study aimed to develop an easy-to-use and practical CXI based on fat-free mass index (FFMI-CXI) to evaluate the prognostic value of FFMI-CXI in CRC.

pmc-11690177.title: TESTING THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN PSYCHOTROPICS AND OPIOIDS WITH FUNCTION IN HOSPITALIZED OLDER ADULTS WITH DEMENTIA
pmc-11690177.creator: Nayeon Kim, Barbara Resnick
pmc-11690177.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The aim of this study was to test if the use of psychotropic medications (antipsychotics, sedatives, antiseizure, antidepressants, and anxiolytics) and opioids were associated with physical function in hospitalized older adults living with dementia. This study was a secondary data analysis using baseline data from the Function Focused Care for Acute Care Using the Evidence Integration Triangle (FFC-AC-EIT) study, which is an ongoing randomized controlled trial. The first 369 participants were included.

pmc-12640979.title: Pathophysiological mechanisms of functional dyspepsia: a narrative review
pmc-12640979.creator: Li Wang, YuPeng Shi, YaNi Li, XiaoJuan Wang, LiJuan Xu, Yue Zhang
pmc-12640979.description: BackgroundFunctional dyspepsia (FD) is a common gastrointestinal disorder with a global prevalence of about 40%. Its pathogenesis is multifactorial and not fully understood, which complicates diagnosis and treatment. Advances in research have improved understanding of the mechanisms underlying FD, offering opportunities to refine diagnosis and therapy.

pmc-13220420.title: Interrupted suture vs continuous suture for primary closure of the common bile duct after laparoscopic common bile duct exploration in patients with choledocholithiasis
pmc-13220420.creator: Tailai An, Yan Wang, Lingna Deng, Yawei Wang, Linsen Liu
pmc-13220420.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeWe performed the present study to compare the interrupted suture technique and the continuous suture technique after laparoscopic common bile duct exploration (LCBDE) for choledocholithiasis.MethodsClinical data from patients with choledocholithiasis who underwent LCBDE were retrospectively collected. Patients were divided into an interrupted suture group and a continuous suture group on the basis of the method used to suture the common bile duct.

pmc-13259183.title: Oral Mycobiome Alterations in Children with Phenylketonuria: Associations with Dietary Intake and Metabolic Context—A Pilot Study
pmc-13259183.creator: Małgorzata Ostrowska, Elwira Komoń-Janczara, Bożena Mikołuć, Katarzyna Iłowiecka, Justyna Jarczak, Justyna Zagórska, Paulina Zambrzycka, Silvia Turroni, Hubert Szczerba
pmc-13259183.description: Background: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is a metabolic disorder requiring a strict low-phenylalanine diet. Oral health impairment, including bacteriome dysbiosis, is common in PKU, yet the mycobiome remains poorly defined. This pilot study aimed to characterise the salivary oral mycobiome of children with PKU compared with controls and to explore associations with dietary intake.

pmc-13411930.title: TranExamic Atomized for Pediatric post-Operative Tonsillectomy hemorrhage (TEAPOT): Study protocol for a pilot randomized controlled trial
pmc-13411930.creator: Andrew D. Meyer, Whitney Schwarz, Dylan Erwin, Marisa Earley, Venkata K. Yellepeddi, Thomas H. Chun, T. Charles Casper, Daniel K. Nishijima, Alejandro Torrado Pacheco, Alejandro Torrado Pacheco

pmc-13499505.title: Network Model to Predict Age‐Related Transcriptional Reprogramming
pmc-13499505.creator: Tyler J. McNeill, Fabrisia Ambrosio, Hirotaka Iijima
pmc-13499505.description: Understanding how secreted factors from aged tissue, often referred to as the senescence‐associated secretome, reshape cellular phenotypes remains a major challenge due to the complexity of downstream molecular cascades. Here, we present a computational framework for in silico perturbation modeling designed to predict distinct transcriptional responses to age‐specific extracellular environmental cues.

pmc-13554992.title: Alterations of gut microbiota in Down syndrome and their association with Alzheimer's disease
pmc-13554992.creator: Camilla Pellegrini, Francesco Ravaioli, Sara De Fanti, Alessia Siliquini, Claudia Sala, Magali Rochat, Virginia Pollarini, Barbara Polischi, Alberto Pasti, Margherita Grasso, Maria Rambaldi, Francesco Cardoni, Nicola Grotteschi, Filippo Caraci, Pietro Cortelli, Federica Provini, Raffaele Lodi, Luca
pmc-13554992.description: INTRODUCTIONAdults with Down syndrome (DS) have a higher risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD). As gut microbiota (GM) alterations have been reported in AD, we investigated their association with cognitive decline and plasma AD biomarkers in DS.METHODSFecal and plasma samples were collected from 58 adults with DS (21–75 years) and 30 euploid controls (CTRL; 25–83 years).

pmc-13569202.title: Screening Equine Skin and Mucous Membranes for Carriage of Coagulase‐Positive Staphylococci
pmc-13569202.creator: Christina M. Dierkes, Daniel O. Morris, Christine L. Cain, Laurel E. Redding, Maho Okumura, Alison Gore, Stephen D. Cole
pmc-13569202.description: BackgroundCommensal populations of coagulase‐positive Staphylococcus spp. (CoPS) in healthy horses are not well‐defined.ObjectiveTo determine the point prevalence, anatomical distribution, antimicrobial susceptibility and genomic characteristics of CoPS in healthy horses.AnimalsOne‐hundred and fifty privately owned, systemically healthy horses from seven facilities were enrolled in this study.Materials and MethodsHorses were sampled from the nares, buccal mucosa and three skin sites.

uslaw-usc-t18-s3574.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part II (Criminal Procedure); Chapter 227 (Sentences); Subchapter C (Fines). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The implementation of a sentence to pay a fine is governed by the provisions of subchapter B of chapter 229.

uslaw-usc-t49-s31135.title: 49 U.S.C. § 31135 — Duties of employers and employees
uslaw-usc-t49-s31135.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t49-s31135.description: United States Code, Title 49 (Transportation); Part B (Commercial); Chapter 311 (Commercial Motor Vehicle Safety); Subchapter III (Safety Regulation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— Each employer and employee shall comply with regulations on commercial motor vehicle safety prescribed by the Secretary of Transportation under this subchapter that apply to the employer’s or employee’s conduct. (b) Noncompliance.— (1) Motor carriers.—.
